abstract_summary: Open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding enables object localization and segmentation from free-form text queries without a fixed category vocabulary. Many recent methods build on 3D Gaussian Splatting and consolidate multi-view observations, such as masked crops from individual views, into language features or compac...

To address this limitation, we proposeEviSplat, which keeps individual observation features avail-
able for query-dependent selection. Using LaGa's class-agnostic grouping (Cen et al., 2025b), EviS-
plat organizes these features into instance observation banks (Fig. 1, bottom). Since different obser-
vations may cover different subsets of an instance's Gaussians, an instance-level score alone cannot
distinguish where query-relevant cues are supported. EviSplat therefore learns an appearance dis-
tribution for each Gaussian to capture its locally supported evidence. Given a query, query-guided
evidence aggregation forms an instance-level score from the most relevant observations and refines
each Gaussian's score with local evidence weighted by observation reliability.
We evaluate EviSplat on LERF-OVS, 3D-OVS, and ScanNet for

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Benchmark metrics use external ground-truth mask and point annotations that are separate from the training loss and query-time scoring.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by mIoU and mAcc against ground-truth human annotations on LERF-OVS, 3D-OVS, and ScanNet.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The evidence field is trained by cross-entropy against empirical prototype distributions derived from unsupervised clustering of multi-view CLIP features, with no text queries or label vocabulary involved.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of superior open-vocabulary segmentation performance and the benefit of retaining multi-view evidence over pre-query consolidation are solidly backed by empirical gains across benchmarks (e.g., 70.7 vs 63.6 baseline mIoU on LERF-OVS) and detailed ablations.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation spans standard open-vocabulary benchmarks including LERF-OVS, 3D-OVS, and ScanNet under both rendered-view and 3D point-level protocols. It provides extensive controlled component analyses, seed variance reporting, and ablation of storage and perturbation sensitivity.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on established ground-truth 2D mask and 3D point annotations that are entirely external and separate from the training loss.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark evaluation metrics (mIoU and mAcc) computed against ground-truth human annotations on LERF-OVS, 3D-OVS, and ScanNet.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss against empirical prototype distributions derived from unsupervised clustering of multi-view CLIP embeddings, completely independent of test text queries and annotations.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge dependencies on source 2D mask segmentations and frozen CLIP representations, as well as limitations in handling complex attribute combinations and spatial relationships.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly articulated, outlining instance observation banking, Gaussian-to-observation association weighting, prototype codebook construction, and evidence-distribution distillation via latent vectors. Query-guided aggregation is rigorously formalized with fixed-mass prototype scoring and reliability-weighted fusion.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides a well-motivated architectural enhancement to 3D Gaussian Splatting for open-vocabulary tasks with thorough ablation studies, transparent implementation details, and solid benchmarking against state-of-the-art baselines.
primary.scoped_contribution: EviSplat introduces an open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that preserves individual multi-view observation features in instance banks and learns a Gaussian-local evidence field, dynamically aggregating query-relevant visual evidence at query time.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper provides a well-motivated architectural enhancement to 3D Gaussian Splatting for open-vocabulary tasks with thorough ablation studies, transparent implementation details, and solid benchmarking against state-of-the-art baselines.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge dependencies on source 2D mask segmentations and frozen CLIP representations, as well as limitations in handling complex attribute combinations and spatial relationships.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

relation_to_agentic_memory.value: Segmentation task adjacent to detection; shares backbones and dense-prediction evaluation

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to computer-vision research based on screening evidence.
